mirror_note: Added after the freeze (2026-09-24): the same frozen breadth-v1 content, not a new version. The partitions are byte-identical (sha256 in `files`) and live only in this private mirror because several sources do not allow public redistribution (SATA-Bench CC-BY-NC-4.0, SGD CC-BY-SA-4.0, Humicroedit with no licence, cfcolor with a code-only notice). Only this manifest is in git; scripts/build_breadth_v1.py rebuilds the partitions byte for byte and the manifest without this entry.

musr.attribution: Sprague et al., MuSR: Testing the Limits of Chain-of-thought with Multistep Soft Reasoning (ICLR 2024)
musr.label_provenance: by construction (the story generator's ground truth), published answer_index
musr.native_splits: one 756-item set; split into halves by item
musr.mapping: state = the narrative; one choice over the published options in published order (keys opt_1..), instructions = the published question; strata = the three subsets (murder mystery, object placements, team allocation)

sata_bench.licence: CC-BY-NC-4.0 (dataset card; the GitHub repo is MIT): the derived records inherit the non-commercial term
sata_bench.attribution: Xu et al., SATA-Bench: Select All That Apply Benchmark for Multiple Choice Questions (2025)
sata_bench.label_provenance: source answer groups (human-labelled multi-answer items pooled by the authors)
sata_bench.native_splits: one 1,604-item set; split into halves by item
sata_bench.mapping: state = passage + question (HTML tags removed); one noul per candidate answer ('Is "X" a correct answer?'), answers and distractors in a seeded order; scored case-exact (every noul right), as the Index does; items with more than 10 candidates or a candidate that is both answer and distractor are dropped

chessbench.licence: Apache-2.0 (code and data release); positions from lichess.org (CC0)
chessbench.attribution: Ruoss et al., Amortized Planning with Large-Scale Transformers: A Case Study on Chess (NeurIPS 2024)
chessbench.label_provenance: engine: Stockfish 16 win probability of every legal move (the test action-value file)
chessbench.native_splits: test action-value file only; split into halves by position
chessbench.mapping: state = FEN, side to move and an ASCII board; one choice over up to 10 legal moves (UCI keys, described as piece, from-to, capture, promotion): the best move plus up to 9 others drawn in a seeded order, leaving out any move within 0.01 win probability of the best so the reference answer is unique; strata = game phase by piece count

contractnli.licence: CC-BY-4.0 (Hitachi America terms of use grant CC BY 4.0)
contractnli.attribution: Koreeda and Manning, ContractNLI: A Dataset for Document-level Natural Language Inference for Contracts (Findings of EMNLP 2021)
contractnli.label_provenance: human (expert annotation of each hypothesis on each NDA)
contractnli.native_splits: development partition from dev.json, test from test.json
contractnli.mapping: state = the full NDA text (no truncation; longer documents are not admitted); up to 4 of the 17 fixed hypotheses per document, drawn round-robin over the three labels, each a choice entailment / contradiction / not_mentioned

hellaswag.licence: MIT (code/data release); ActivityNet Captions contexts only
hellaswag.attribution: Zellers et al., HellaSwag: Can a Machine Really Finish Your Sentence? (ACL 2019)
hellaswag.native_splits: validation only (test labels are hidden); split into halves by source video
hellaswag.mapping: ActivityNet-derived items only (source_id activitynet~...): the WikiHow-derived half is left out because wikiHow's 2026-09-14 DMCA notice took down the HellaSwag GitHub repository (github/dmca 2026-09-14-wikihow.md); state = activity label + context; one choice over the four endings in published order; strata = in-domain / zero-shot

clinc150.attribution: Larson et al., An Evaluation Dataset for Intent Classification and Out-of-Scope Prediction (EMNLP 2019)
clinc150.label_provenance: crowdsourced utterances written for each intent (published label)
clinc150.native_splits: plus config: development from validation, test from test
clinc150.mapping: state = the utterance; one choice over 10 options: an in-scope utterance gets its intent plus 8 other intents of the same domain (clinc/oos-eval domains.json) plus out_of_scope; an out-of-scope utterance gets 9 intents of one seeded domain plus out_of_scope (always last); strata = the 10 domains and out-of-scope

sgd.licence: CC-BY-SA-4.0: the derived records inherit the share-alike term
sgd.attribution: Rastogi et al., Towards Scalable Multi-domain Conversational Agents: The Schema-Guided Dialogue Dataset (AAAI 2020); Lee et al., SGD-X (AAAI 2022)
sgd.label_provenance: human-annotated dialogue state (active_intent of the user turn's frame)
sgd.native_splits: development from dev dialogues, test from test dialogues
sgd.mapping: one user turn per dialogue: state = the service description and the dialogue up to and including that turn; one choice over the service's intents (name: description) plus NONE; the schema wording is the original or one of the five SGD-X paraphrase variants, chosen per dialogue by hash; strata = NONE / intent changed / intent unchanged since the previous user turn; turns with more than one frame are skipped

bright.attribution: Su et al., BRIGHT: A Realistic and Challenging Benchmark for Reasoning-Intensive Retrieval (ICLR 2025)
bright.label_provenance: human (StackExchange answers' cited documents, annotated gold chunks)
bright.native_splits: examples only; split into halves by query
bright.mapping: StackExchange domains only (biology, earth_science, economics, psychology, robotics, stackoverflow, sustainable_living); state = the post; one choice over 5 document chunks: one gold chunk and the 4 highest-BM25 chunks of the same domain that are not gold, not excluded and not from a gold document's page, every option 150-1,500 characters, in a seeded order; strata = domain

bfcl.attribution: Patil et al., The Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL) (ICML 2025)
bfcl.label_provenance: human-verified ground-truth calls (possible_answer); irrelevance categories call nothing
bfcl.native_splits: one set per category; split into halves by item
bfcl.mapping: state = the conversation and every supplied function (name, description, JSON parameters); one noul per function 'Should the assistant call `name`?' (true when the ground truth calls it), at most 10 functions; scored case-exact, as the Index does; strata = the ten single-turn AST categories (simple, multiple, parallel, parallel_multiple, irrelevance and their live_ versions)

toolret.licence: Apache-2.0 (ToolRet release); queries and tools re-published from its source benchmarks
toolret.attribution: Shi et al., Retrieval Models Aren't Tool-Savvy: Benchmarking Tool Retrieval for Large Language Models (Findings of ACL 2025)
toolret.native_splits: queries only; split into halves by query
toolret.mapping: subsets except apibank (API-Bank is its own dataset in this panel), apigen (Salesforce xLAM-60k, whose card carries a research-only statement); state = the query; one choice over 5 tools (name: description, description cut to 400 characters): one labelled tool and the 4 highest-BM25 unlabelled tools of the same tool corpus (web / code / customized), in a seeded order; strata = subset

apibank.attribution: Li et al., API-Bank: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Tool-Augmented LLMs (EMNLP 2023)
apibank.native_splits: level-1 test only; split into halves by dialogue file
apibank.mapping: state = the dialogue so far; one choice over up to 8 APIs (name: description): the APIs the level-1 item itself describes plus the highest-BM25 others from the level-1 catalog, in a seeded order; strata = the reference API

routerbench.attribution: Hu et al., RouterBench: A Benchmark for Multi-LLM Routing System (2024), Martian
routerbench.label_provenance: recorded correctness of each model's answer (0/1 exact scoring by the RouterBench harness)
routerbench.native_splits: 0-shot file only; split into halves by sample
routerbench.mapping: MMLU, Winogrande and MBPP prompts whose 11 scores are all 0/1 (GSM8K is left out because its scores in this file are fractional, HellaSwag for the wikiHow notice, ARC because ARC is in Kev's training data); state = the prompt; one choice 'which of these models answered correctly' over one correct model and up to 9 incorrect ones (drawn in a seeded order), so the answer is unique; strata = source benchmark

humicroedit.licence: none stated (SemEval-2020 Task 7 research release; the README asks users to cite the task paper)
humicroedit.attribution: Hossain et al., SemEval-2020 Task 7: Assessing Humor in Edited News Headlines (SemEval 2020)
humicroedit.label_provenance: human (crowd funniness grades; label = the edit with the higher mean grade)
humicroedit.mapping: state = the original headline; one choice between the two edited headlines (a / b), ties dropped; one pair per headline; strata = label

cfcolor.licence: release notice: 'Permission is granted for anyone to copy, use, modify, or distribute this program and accompanying programs and documents for any purpose' (runPrediction.m), no separate data licence
cfcolor.attribution: O'Donovan, Agarwala and Hertzmann, Collaborative Filtering of Color Aesthetics (CAe 2014)
cfcolor.native_splits: one rating set; split into halves by user
cfcolor.mapping: one record per user: state = 12 of the user's training-set ratings (five hex colours and a 1-5 rating each); one choice between two palettes from the user's test-set ratings with different ratings, which did this person rate higher (a / b); strata = label

gpqa_diamond.reason: gated on the Hub (Idavidrein/gpqa: accepting the dataset's terms is required, and this account has not); not accepted on the owner's behalf. Its terms also ask that examples not be revealed in plain text online, which a public suite would do

decision_index.formula: per benchmark k = clip((score - chance) / (1 - chance)) on the coverage-adjusted score (unanswered = wrong); area = mean of its benchmarks; index = 100 x mean of the five areas

chessbench.name: ChessBench
chessbench.subset_rule: 5,000 of 61,833 prepared cases, deterministic hash sample without replacement (seed 20260919); no outcome-based selection.

sgd.name: SGD/SGD-X
sgd.subset_rule: 2,500 of 46,116 prepared cases, deterministic hash sample without replacement (seed 20260919); no outcome-based selection.

bright.name: BRIGHT
bright.subset_rule: 550 of 1,297 scoreable v1 queries kept (637 requests): stratified by source domain, proportional allocation with at least one query per domain (seed 20260922); kept queries keep their complete candidate lists; no outcome-based selection.

toolret.name: ToolRet
toolret.subset_rule: 1,000 of 7,704 scoreable v1 queries kept (1,328 requests): stratified by source domain, proportional allocation with at least one query per domain (seed 20260922); kept queries keep their complete candidate lists; no outcome-based selection.

routerbench.name: RouterBench
routerbench.subset_rule: 10,000 requests within a 10,000-request cap: 5,001 complete linked case groups of 29,163 prepared; groups kept intact.

cfcolor.name: cfcolor
cfcolor.subset_rule: 5,000 of 11,821 prepared cases, deterministic hash sample without replacement (seed 20260919); no outcome-based selection.

metrics.case_exact: fraction of records with every question right

scoring.chance: expected score of uniform random answers: mean of 1/K over questions (accuracy), mean over records of the product of 1/K (case_exact)
scoring.skill: clip((score - chance) / (1 - chance)) with unanswered questions scored wrong; area = mean of its datasets; index = 100 x mean of the five areas
scoring.calibration: ECE (10 bins) and Brier on the returned probabilities of answered questions, per dataset, area and pooled

context.note: records are admitted at `admission` under the tokenizer above (row = state + one question <= 7,680 tokens) and scored in the serving context; far longer than Kev's 384 / 1,024 training context

selection: development and test 150 records per dataset (40 documents for contractnli); native dev/test splits kept where they exist, otherwise groups dealt to halves in a seeded hash order; round-robin over each dataset's strata in a seeded order; normalised-text state dedupe across all datasets and both partitions (test first); no group spans the partitions
label_protocol: no LLM labels: every label is the source dataset's own (human, engine, recorded execution or by construction); candidate subsets always contain the reference answer

excluded_subsets.apibank: API-Bank is its own dataset in this panel
excluded_subsets.apigen: Salesforce xLAM-60k, whose card carries a research-only statement

large_partitions: partitions with in_git false are gitignored; upload them to the Hub mirror (kev.suite.SUITES_DATASET) and bump SUITES_REVISION before load_split can fetch them elsewhere
